brief_data.deck: Moove, the fleet operator that runs Waymo's all-electric Jaguar I-PACE robotaxis in Phoenix and Miami and is Waymo's named partner for London, announced a $250M Series C at a $2.1B valuation on 5 August, led by Mubadala and co-led by Toyota's Woven Capital and Ion Pacific.

risks.label: NOT A RACE INPUT
risks.detail: Depots and charging orchestration give the team nothing to use; a halo at a manufacturer team can read as a logo.
risks.counter: Anchor the deal on the I-PACE fleets and the two matching rounds; keep the activation about cars, not depots.

risks.label: CAPITAL GOES TO FLEETS
risks.detail: The round funds owning autonomous vehicles outright, a capital-intensive plan that competes with marketing spend.
risks.counter: Size the entry small and value-in-kind heavy: fleet livery and rider activations cost Moove little.

extended.ask: A 25-minute call with Ladi Delano before Jaguar closes its Season 13 roster to agree a London E-Prix announcement window and size an Official Fleet Partner entry built around the Miami and London rounds.

value.text: Depots and charging orchestration are not a race-car input, and the brief says so. The value is commercial: a Jaguar-branded robotaxi story during race weeks at Miami and London, rider-to-race activations where Waymo riders are taken to the E-Prix in the cars, and a road-EV proof point the racing programme was built to promote.
value.label: Halo with mechanics (Mode B)

value.text: Moove's investors and partners, Mubadala, Toyota's Woven Capital, Uber and Waymo, are the mobility and sovereign-capital audience Jaguar's other partners want in the suite at Miami and London.
value.label: Commercial lift for the team

value.text: Driver appearances at Nest openings, a depot-to-grid content series on charging and energy management, and a reference story Moove can use with every city regulator it approaches.
value.label: Content and ecosystem

value.text: Official Fleet Partner designation, sidepod placement, hospitality at the Miami and London rounds, rights to co-brand I-PACE fleet livery on race weeks, driver and engineering access for Moove's channels.
value.label: What the team gives back

why_now.text: On 5 August Mubadala and Moove announced a $250M Series C at a $2.1B valuation, led by Mubadala Investment Company and co-led by Woven Capital, Toyota's growth fund, and Ion Pacific, with BlueCrest and Sona Capital new alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton, Uber and the Ontario Power Generation Pension Plan. It is a lead-investor release, carried the same day by BusinessWire, TechCrunch and The National.
why_now.label: Trigger

why_now.text: Moove reports about $420M of annual recurring revenue from roughly 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries, built organically and through the acquisitions of Kovi in Brazil and Tokyo Taxi in Japan. The proceeds fund autonomous fleet ownership and 'Nests', robotics-first depots where robotaxis are charged, serviced and orchestrated, with the autonomous workforce growing from about 150 to about 500 by the end of 2026.
why_now.label: Scale behind it

why_now.text: Waymo named Moove its fleet partner for London in October 2025, its first European city, operating and maintaining all-electric Jaguar I-PACEs; testing is under way under a government-backed pilot and commercial service is pending regulatory approval. A brand launching driverless Jaguars in London wants to be known there before the cars arrive.
why_now.label: The London launch

why_now.text: Season 13 opens in Jeddah on 18 December and teams close rosters this autumn. The Miami E-Prix on 20 February and the London E-Prix double-header on 29-30 May 2027 are Moove's two Waymo cities; the Austin E-Prix on 6 February adds a third US stage.
why_now.label: Calendar window

why_team.text: Waymo's Phoenix and Miami fleets that Moove operates and maintains are all-electric Jaguar I-PACEs, and the London fleet will be too. No other team on either grid has its road car in Moove's daily operation.
why_team.label: The cars Moove runs

why_team.text: Per the sponsor table, Jaguar TCS Racing carries TCS as title partner, Castrol and Jaguar itself, and no fleet, mobility or ride-hail partner; nor does any other Formula E roster. Official Fleet Partner is a clean category.
why_team.label: The open lane

why_team.text: Jaguar has committed to the GEN4 era, Seasons 13-16 through 2030, so a three-year deal sits inside a confirmed programme, and the London E-Prix is the team's home round in the city where Moove's next launch happens.
why_team.label: Platform that lasts

why_team.text: Jaguar's Formula E programme exists to sell electric road cars; tens of thousands of driverless I-PACE hours a week in three cities is the most visible real-world use of that car anywhere, and Moove is the operator.
why_team.label: Road-to-race proof

ruled_out.reason: US team with Miami and Austin rounds, but no vehicle tie; TWG AI and Quest Global fill its technology lanes.
Penske Autosport's parent runs its own truck-leasing and fleet businesses; a fleet operator on that car conflicts with the owner.

ruled_out.team: Nissan Formula E Team · Citroën Racing · Porsche Formula E Team · Cupra Kiro
ruled_out.reason: Manufacturer teams whose road cars are not in Moove's Waymo fleets; a Jaguar-fleet operator would sit awkwardly on a rival OEM's car.
Mahindra makes ride-hail vehicles in India, one of Moove's markets; the owner competes with Moove's suppliers.
Open but not chosen: no vehicle, city or partner tie comparable to Jaguar's.

brief_data.bottom_line: A $250M round at $2.1B announced by Mubadala, about $420M of recurring revenue, and Jaguar I-PACE robotaxi fleets in Phoenix, Miami and soon London put Moove at peak brand motive with a unique tie to one team. The lane at Jaguar is open; the halo-only value and fleet capex hold the score at 71.

brief_data.the_case_p1: The round is announced by the lead investor and the company: $250M at $2.1B, led by Mubadala, co-led by Woven Capital and Ion Pacific, with BlueCrest and Sona Capital new alongside BlackRock, MUFG, Franklin Templeton and Uber. Moove reports about $420M of annual recurring revenue from roughly 42,000 vehicles in 29 cities across 13 countries. Proceeds go to owning autonomous fleets outright and to 'Nests', robotics-first depots where robotaxis are charged, serviced and orchestrated, with the autonomous workforce growing from about 150 to about 500 by year-end.
brief_data.the_case_p2: The identity moment is the pivot from financing drivers in Lagos to owning the operating layer beneath robotaxis. Since Waymo contracted Moove for Phoenix and Miami in December 2024, every vehicle it runs there has been a Jaguar I-PACE; London, Waymo's first European city, is next, with Moove as fleet partner and service pending regulators. A company about to put its name on driverless Jaguars in three cities needs a brand its riders, regulators and partners recognise.

brief_data.industry_meta: Mobility Infrastructure · Autonomous & EV Fleet Operations
brief_data.value_content: MODE B - halo with mechanics. Moove's product, depots and charging orchestration for EV fleets, is not a race-car input, so the value is commercial: Official Fleet Partner, a Jaguar-branded robotaxi story in race weeks at Miami and London, rider-to-race activations, and a demonstrable road-EV use of the I-PACE that the racing programme was built to promote. Moove brings Mubadala, Toyota, Uber and Waymo into the Jaguar suite; the team gives livery, hospitality and driver content.
brief_data.why_team_para: Jaguar TCS Racing is the only team whose road car Moove already runs: the Waymo fleets it operates in Phoenix and Miami, and will operate in London, are Jaguar I-PACEs. Jaguar has committed to the GEN4 era through 2030, so the platform outlives a three-year deal. The sponsor table shows TCS as title partner, Castrol and Jaguar itself, and no fleet, mobility or ride-hail partner at Jaguar or on any Formula E roster; the lane is clean and the London E-Prix is the home round.
brief_data.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Fleet Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, spanning the London launch and the fleet-ownership build. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year. Scope: sidepod placement, Miami and London hospitality, co-branded I-PACE fleet livery on race weeks, driver appearances at Nest openings.
brief_data.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The round closed on 5 August and teams close Season 13 rosters this autumn, before the Jeddah opener on 18 December; Moove's two Waymo cities then host the Miami E-Prix on 20 February and the London E-Prix on 29-30 May 2027, and London's driverless launch is due the same season.
brief_data.decision_maker_bio: Delano co-founded Moove in Lagos in 2020, is Co-CEO and separately chairman, and fronts the raises; he is UK-based. Path: Jide Odunsi, Co-Founder and Co-CEO; Tayo Oyegunle, COO; Tingting Peng, Chief Capital, Strategy and Impact Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief_data.opening_angle_intro: Lead with the cars Moove already runs.
brief_data.opening_angle_quote: “Ladi, every Waymo you operate in Phoenix and Miami is a Jaguar, and London is next. Jaguar's race team has no fleet partner and its home race is the London E-Prix. 25 minutes before the roster closes to see the numbers?”
